definitions.explanation: the force that draws objects toward each other, especially gravity

examples.japanese: ⟦{地球|ちきゅう}→地球：03461_chikyuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{引力|いんりょく}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{強|つよ}い→強い：00820_tsuyoi⟧。
⟦{月|つき}→月：02230_tsuki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{引力|いんりょく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{潮|しお}→潮：13369_shio⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{満|み}ち{引|ひ}き⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{影響|えいきょう}→影響：01877_eikyou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The moon's gravitational pull affects the tides.

examples.japanese: ニュートン⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧リンゴ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{落|お}ちる→落ちる：01242_ochiru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}て→見る：00283_miru⟧{万有引力|ばんゆういんりょく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{法則|ほうそく}→法則：05143_housoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{発見|はっけん}した→発見する：26929_hakkensuru⟧。
examples.english: Newton discovered the law of universal gravitation after seeing an apple fall.

notes:
Composed of {引|いん} (pull) + {力|りょく} (force). Primarily a physics term for gravitational attraction, but also used figuratively for the power to draw people or things together.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {万有引力|ばんゆういんりょく}: universal gravitation
- {引力|いんりょく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{法則|ほうそく}→法則：05143_housoku⟧: law of gravitation
- {引力|いんりょく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{働|はたら}く→働く：00503_hataraku⟧: gravity acts/operates
- {引力|いんりょく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{逆|さか}らう→逆らう：02106_sakarau⟧: to defy gravity
- {引力|いんりょく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}ける→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧: to be subject to gravitational pull

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{重力|じゅうりょく}→重力：25301_juuryoku⟧: gravity — the downward pull experienced on a celestial body's surface; more commonly used in everyday contexts
- {引力|いんりょく}: focuses on the mutual attraction between two masses, while ⟦{重力|じゅうりょく}→重力：25301_juuryoku⟧ emphasizes the force pulling things downward
- ⟦{磁力|じりょく}→磁力：17784_jiryoku⟧: magnetic force — attraction or repulsion between magnets
